subject: Post-call: Ember trial — capacity & success criteria (POC scope)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Liang <tom.liang@ember.ai>, Rachel Park <rachel.park@ember.ai>
Cc: Linda Wu <linda.wu@ember.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — Ember trial: proposed success criteria & capacity

Thanks for the productive call earlier — quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have the scope locked before the trial kickoff. I put items below for confirmation; where I’ve noted owners, please correct if I’ve mis-assigned.

POC objective (what success looks like):
- Baseline throughput: support 200 sustained inference requests per minute across peak 1-hour windows with median latency <= 120ms and 95th <= 300ms (prompt mix sent in follow-up).
- Quality: >= 95% pass rate on the 150-step rubric we discussed (intent preservation and hallucination controls) evaluated against Ember-supplied eval set.
- Integration: ability to run production-like traffic via your internal harness using our SDK (no major SDK blockers).

Evaluation plan & ownership:
- Ember: provide anonymized eval dataset + access to the test harness (owner: Tom).
- Redwood: provide evaluation harness runbook, temporary environment, and dashboard access (owner: Vanessa).
- Joint: run three soak windows (2 hours each) with controlled traffic and a cumulative result report.

Timeline (proposed):
- July 20: POC environment ready, kickoff check-in (30m).
- July 21–July 28: daily short runs and two full soak windows (team available for ops).
- July 29: delivery of results and go/no-go decision.

Capacity proposal (initial ask + what we can commit):
- Your ask: capacity to match production-like throughput. You mentioned wanting some reserved baseline.
- Redwood proposal (subject to final confirmation from infra): reserve 4 x A10G-equivalent GPUs as baseline for the trial with autoscale available up to 12 GPUs for burst windows. Autoscale policy: fast-scale to cover short spikes, 30m cooldown for scale-down.
- Expected KV-cache warm-up: assume 10–15 minutes full warm-up for repeated prompt patterns; recommend testing cold vs warm runs.

Commercial / procurement notes:
- We can provide trial credits to offset initial burst usage during evaluation; procurement lead Linda — please share any required PO/compliance steps for billing.

Attachments: ember-poc-success-criteria.xlsx (spreadsheet with rubrics and example prompts).

Next steps:
1) Tom — confirm eval dataset availability and if you want baseline reserved GPUs increased to 6 instead of 4 (reply here).
2) Linda — confirm procurement timeline / PO window.
3) Redwood (Vanessa) — we’ll loop in Sergio and Rishi to finalize the autoscale policy and cost estimate by EOD Jul 14.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the environment live.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

- We can provide the anonymized eval set by EOD Jul 16 — it’s ~2000 inference prompts (mix of short and long contexts). Owner: Rachel.
- On capacity: after checking internally, we’d prefer a baseline reserve of 6 GPUs (to better mirror our prod shape) with ability to burst to 12. Can you confirm pricing delta for 6 vs 4 reserved for a 2-week trial?
- Procurement: We can issue a PO by Jul 25. Linda — I’ll sync separately about any compliance docs you need.

One question: can you confirm whether autoscale will pre-warm KV cache for anticipated traffic patterns during the soak windows? If not, we’ll plan a warmup stage.

If you can confirm the 6-GPU baseline and outline the short cost note, we’ll lock the kickoff for July 20 10:00am PT.

—Tom

Forwarding Tom’s quick reply — Ember is asking to move baseline reserve to 6 GPUs and burst to 12. They’d like confirmation on: autoscale pre-warm behavior, exact cooldown policy, and a short cost delta for 6 vs 4 reserved during a 2-week trial.

Key asks for infra/cost team:
- Can we commit to baseline 6 x A10G-equivalent reserved for the trial window (Jul 20–Jul 29)?
- Autoscale policy we propose: scale up immediately to cover load (seconds-level reaction for queue-backed requests), scale-down with 30-minute cooldown; burst cap 12; allow manual override during soak windows.
- Pre-warm: does Redwood have a mechanism to pre-populate KV cache for the request patterns (yes/no + ops steps)? If not native, what’s the recommended warmup script?
- Short cost delta: one-slide estimate that shows 4->6 reserved delta and expected burst cost for two heavy soak windows.

Can you confirm by EOD so I can reply to Tom and lock kickoff? I’ve attached the original call notes above.

Thanks — Vanessa

Subject: RE: Post-call recap — Ember trial: capacity & success criteria (POC scope) — confirmed capacity and kickoff

Tom / Rachel — quick update with commitments and concrete next steps so you can proceed with internal scheduling.

Capacity commitments (Redwood):
- Reserved baseline: 6 x A10G-equivalent GPUs reserved for the trial window Jul 20 00:00 PT through Jul 29 23:59 PT.
- Autoscale: allowed up to 12 GPUs for burst; autoscale reacts to queue depth and token throughput. Scale-down cooldown 30 minutes. Manual scaling allowed during soak windows.
- Pre-warm: Redwood does not auto pre-populate customer KV cache on scale events. Ops will run a warmup script (included in the attached stub redwood-ember-poc-config-stub.json) to prime frequent prompt patterns; expect ~10–15 minutes to reach steady-state cache hit rates.

Cost & credits:
- Short delta: 4->6 reserved adds approximately $1,200/day for the reserved window (two-week estimate attached as redwood-cost-estimate-ember-poc.pdf). Burst usage will be billed at on-demand burst rates; we will apply $5,000 in trial credits to help absorb initial soak bursts.

Operational items / kickoff:
- Jul 20 10:00am PT — 30m kickoff (agenda: environment check, test harness access, smoke run).
- On Jul 21 we’ll run the first full 2-hour soak window; ops will be oncall (Sergio / Rishi).
- Augmented monitoring: we’ll share a live dashboard link during the soak and provide a post-mortem report 24 hours after each soak.

Attachments: redwood-ember-poc-config-stub.json (warmup script + autoscale knobs), redwood-cost-estimate-ember-poc.pdf (two-week delta + burst example).

Next steps (actionable):
1) Ember: confirm kickoff time Jul 20 10:00am PT (Tom) and that Rachel will share the eval set by Jul 16.
2) Ember: Linda to confirm PO window (Jul 25 target) if you plan to purchase dedicated capacity after trial.
3) Redwood: Sergio & Rishi to join kickoff and share the warmup playbook during the meeting.
4) Vanessa: I’ll create the HubSpot milestone and push the trial playbook link (HubSpot deal ID: 1234567890).

If that all sounds good I’ll lock the calendar invite after Tom confirms.
